exposure: Subcuticular suture for skin closure after caesarean section
Skin staples for skin closure after caesarean section
cohort: A total of 500 patients undergoing caesarean section, randomly divided into two groups for skin closure method.
finding: Subcuticular suture for skin closure after caesarean section resulted in a significantly lower frequency of wound infection (7.2%) compared to skin staples (14.4%).
mod_finding: Subcuticular sutures for skin closure after caesarean delivery were associated with significantly less wound infection compared to staples.
gest_age: Mean gestational age was 38.60 ± 1.23 weeks in the suture group and 38.71 ± 1.33 weeks in the staples group.
